subject: Priv deploy: module consolidation + networking gap analysis
messages:
From: Emily Park <emily@acmecloud.com>
To: dylan_brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@acmecloud.com
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: private deployment module consolidation & security gaps

Hi Dylan,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. We kicked off an internal review of the private deployment artifacts you shared (Terraform modules, Helm charts, Ansible playbooks) and have a short list of concerns we'd like your team to review prior to a pilot:

- Network segregation: our security team wants clearer subnet ownership across control plane vs inference nodes; current diagram mixes overlay and pod CIDRs.
- Secrets lifecycle: we need one recommended KMS pattern and rotation policy for Helm/Ansible steps.
- CI gate evidence: can you provide a list of required CI checks/result artifacts we can consume for our audit (e.g., plan diffs, module unit tests, image SBOMs)?
- Module consolidation: your modules for vpc, routing, and fw_rules have overlapping variables and duplicate logic; we'd prefer a small set of composable modules.

I've attached our initial notes and a redline of the network diagram (network-diagram-v2.png + tf-modules-review.pdf). Can we do a targeted review session this week with your infra leads (30–45m)? Chris from Infra-Consulting will join to advise.

Thanks,
Emily Park
Infrastructure Architect
Acme Cloud Solutions

Attachments: tf-modules-review.pdf (8 pages), network-diagram-v2.png (1 file)
From: dylan_brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Park <emily@acmecloud.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, hiro_tanaka <hiro.tanaka@redwood.ai>, monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 12:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: private deployment module consolidation & security gaps

Emily —

Appreciate the detailed notes and the diagram redlines. We can run a focused session Thursday 10:00–10:45 PT; please confirm and we'll send a calendar invite. Quick reactions inline below, will follow with a short prep doc: 

- Network segregation: agree — our current example overlay was simplified for docs. For production we recommend separate VPCs for control plane, infer nodes, and management (jump boxes/logging). We also have an option that uses routed subnets + NVA for stricter egress control.
- Secrets lifecycle: we support two patterns in our private repo: KMS-backed Helm secrets + ephemeral Ansible vault for bootstrapping. Rotation is documented but we can centralize the guidance (KMS key rotation + automated secret refresh job).
- CI gate evidence: we can produce a minimal checklist: terraform fmt/check, plan with module diffs, tfsec scan, module unit tests (terratest), helm lint + chart-testing, image SBOMs, signed artifact hash. I'll attach a draft matrix (ci-gating-checklist.xlsx).
- Module consolidation: I agree some variable duplication crept in across iterations. We propose a consolidation plan: core-vpc (network primitives), routing (NAT/NGW), security (fw rules/sgs) consuming shared common-vars module. We can show proposed refactor in the review session.

Cc'ing Laura (network lead) and Hiro (platform infra) to prepare the module diffs and environment-specific guidance. Monica will coordinate the calendar + audit artifacts.

Thanks — talk soon.

—Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: dylan_brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: hiro.tanaka <hiro.tanaka@redwood.ai>, monica.patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Emily Park <emily@acmecloud.com>, Chris Lang <chris.lang@infra-consult.com>
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Re: Request: private deployment module consolidation & security gaps

Forwarding my prep notes for the session — I've also attached a quick network appendix and an export of the current module graph. Please review ahead:

--- Forwarded prep notes ---
From: laura_bennett
1) Proposed network segmentation (summary):
   - control-plane-vpc: API endpoints, policy controllers, k8s control plane nodes (private subnets only).
   - inference-vpc: inference GPU/NIC-attached instances, dedicated EKS nodes or VM pool.
   - management-vpc: bastion, CI runners, log collectors with strict peering and VPC endpoints.
   - egress: restricted through NAT + NVA where required; optional proxy for telemetry.

2) Terraform module reorg plan (high level):
   - commons/vars: central variable definitions, tagging, provider aliasing.
   - vpc-core: CIDR allocation, AZ-aware subnets, route tables.
   - networking-routing: NGW/NAT, Transit GW attachments when multi-VPC.
   - security-policy: network ACL templates, security groups, managed fw rules (iptables/NSG templates for on-prem).
   - helm-charts: chart library + values schema; move secrets references to values file with KMS-backed secrets manager integration.

3) CI/CD gating checklist (deliverables for audit):
   - plan artifacts with module diff (retained for 90 days)
   - automated tfsec/tflint reports
   - module unit tests + coverage badges
   - helm chart schema tests, signed charts in artifact registry

4) Gaps we want to address during session:
   - explicit KMS key rotation policy and audit trail (ACME wants retention windows).
   - a proven pattern for on-prem subnet mapping to physical NICs / VLANs in the Helm values.
   - a clear rollback mechanism for config drift in the private stack.

Attachments: module-graph.svg (embedded), network-appendix.pdf

--- end forwarded prep notes ---

Laura
Laura Bennett
Network Lead, Redwood Inference
From: dylan_brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Park <emily@acmecloud.com>, Chris Lang <chris.lang@infra-consult.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, hiro_tanaka <hiro.tanaka@redwood.ai>, monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 5 Aug 2026 16:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Priv deploy: module consolidation + networking gap analysis — follow ups & action items

Thanks all for the meeting today — good alignment. Capturing action items and owners below so we have a single source of truth: 

1) Module refactor PRs: Dylan & Hiro to open RFC + initial refactor branch by Fri 2026-08-07. PR will include migration notes and deprecation plan for old module variables. (owner: dylan_brooks, hiro_tanaka)
2) KMS rotation & evidence: Monica to draft KMS rotation policy + automated rotation job runbook; deliverable for Acme audit by 2026-08-11. (owner: monica_patel)
3) CI artifacts: Dylan to publish CI gating checklist (ci-gating-checklist.xlsx) to shared drive and add sample pipeline snippet that collects plan artifacts, tfsec output, and SBOM. (owner: dylan_brooks)
4) On-prem mapping: Laura to produce a one-page mapping for VLAN/NIC <> Helm values and an example playbook for Ansible to wire physical interfaces. (owner: laura_bennett)
5) Follow-up session: 2026-08-12 09:00 PT to review PR and evidence bundle. Emily/Chris to confirm.

Open questions flagged during the meeting:
- Acme asked whether rollback can be automated in the event of a bad module deploy; we have a manual rollback doc today. Need to propose an automated canary + fast rollback pattern.
- Audit retention windows — Acme requires 90 days for plan artifacts, but we'd like to standardize on 180 days for enterprise customers.

Next steps: I'll open a shared folder and upload the PR template + checklist this evening. If anyone has additional artifacts (terratest examples, SBOM generator), drop them in the folder and ping the thread.

-Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: ci-gating-checklist.xlsx; links uploaded to https://drive.redwood.internal/d/1A2b_tf-modules-review
